content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to using [company_name] [product_name]. I'm currently trying to use [product_name] [version_no] to write to a coil register on another device via Modbus, utilizing the network output block. When I tested this setup, there was no effect on the target device. My program sends a logical high to the network output block, with the coil as the address. I tried following a video on this topic ([url]), but it didn't work for me. My main goal is to activate a single coil on the Modbus device. Everything works fine using a Modbus simulation tool on my computer, but not through [product_name]. Ping diagnostics show the device as connected, but nothing changes on the actual device. Have I missed a step in configuring this?

I've attached a sample project demonstrating my approach. Please ensure you match the IP addresses of both devices to your own configuration. Modbus access must be enabled in the file properties of [product_name], with [product_name] set as the client.
Unfortunately, I'm unable to open the file you sent; it shows an "Unknown error" when attempting to open.
Which version of the software are you using? I was able to load the program without issue. Try launching the LSC application first, then select the program to open.
I'm running [product_name] [version_no] on Linux and attempted to open the file via File -> Open in [product_name].

Please check your exact software version. The latest update was in February 2022: [version_no] SP1 Update 1. Also, try launching the LSC application first before opening the project file. Compatibility issues might occur on Linux. If you'd like, share your own test program and we can see if it opens correctly on the Windows version.
I'll attempt a software update, thank you!
I've now updated to [version_no], but I'm still experiencing the same issue.
I created the project in LSC [version_no]. I'm able to open the project file without any problem.
I tried to open the project using LSC [version_no], but receive the same error.
Sorry, I can't assist further in this case— the file seems okay. Please submit a support request.

I've used both a standard input and a logical high input, with matching IP addresses. The Modbus simulation program works perfectly on my computer, but not with the PLC. Is there any way to debug further? I considered using WireShark to monitor local network traffic, but there doesn't appear to be any data sent from the PLC to the Modbus device.

It's possible that your software isn't functioning properly. As suggested above, please reach out to [company_name] through the "Support Request" option. It's helpful to add your own project file— this will be beneficial if a forum volunteer is able to review it. However, the issue may persist if the software itself is faulty.
Have you enabled Modbus access? Go to File > Properties > Offline Settings > General.

Just wanted to share that I resolved my issue. For instance, if I tried to send to register address 10, the [product_name] would actually send to address 9. To communicate with address 10, I have to enter address 11 instead. The manual didn't mention this, so hopefully this helps others facing a similar situation.
It's a known behavior that [product_name] applies a +1 offset when handling Modbus addresses.
I wasn't aware of this offset, and couldn't find it documented in the [product_name] manual. At least it's working now, which is a relief.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face difficulties writing to a Modbus-compatible device using [product_name] PLC and [product_name] software on Linux. While connectivity tests are successful, direct Modbus coil writes fail. Additionally, users encounter errors opening project files in [product_name] on Linux, despite upgrading to the latest version. Meanwhile, the same files open correctly on Windows, highlighting potential platform compatibility issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] project files to open consistently on Linux and for the [product_name] PLC to perform Modbus coil writes as intended, matching the reliability seen in tutorials and guidance from others.
